I'm returning **PASS** on candidate `sha256:d3743a352912a357b0a81124794561cea5f06f5dbc31542b9623c68c47649ab7` (frozen at commit `a6bdea0`), with **no new findings**.

**Candidate check.** HEAD is `2cfbf4f`, one commit after the freeze, and it only adds the round-7 assignments, the manifest and `stages.json`. Those files are left out of the candidate ID by design. The candidate ID recomputes to the same value here and in a clean full clone at `a6bdea0`, and the lockfile is byte-identical.

**Checks** (all run in a throwaway clone, which I've deleted):
- **What changed since round 6:** only `architecture.testkit.ts` and `architecture.test.ts`. Both are left out of the production build, and the build output contains no architecture file. Nothing else changed in the product, API contract, data model, ADRs, source documents or translations. The requirements register is unchanged.
- **Unit tests:** 271 of 271 pass (one more than round 6: the new sqlite check A1). The module-boundary suite has 78 tests, matching the count D-053 claims. The translation and glossary tests pass 19 of 19.
- **The new `node:sqlite` ban (F-DG1-127) doesn't reach too far.** I compared the round-6 and round-7 import rules over 108 module names. The only name whose verdict changes is `node:sqlite`. Bare `sqlite` was already refused in round 6, because only declared dependencies are allowed.
  - All 47 legitimate imports are still allowed, and the real module tree has 0 violations.
  - All 9 ways of importing sqlite are caught.
  - No production code uses sqlite, and storage is PostgreSQL per ADR-0003.
  - My first probe run failed because I wrongly expected bare `sqlite` to change too. That was my mistake, not a candidate defect. I kept that output and recorded the fix in the evidence.
- **Accepted limits (D-053):** the testkit header and D-053 say plainly that the check is a static safeguard with known gaps, "NOT a runtime security boundary", and not proven complete. That's an honest description, and nothing in it changes what users see.
- **Integration:** two runs, each on a fresh throwaway PostgreSQL 16. Both passed 200 of 200, left no stray databases and logged no FATAL errors. They covered:
  - closing a transformation by status edit is refused with 422;
  - page cursors are tied to their filter and sort;
  - the login (OIDC) state, nonce, PKCE and CSRF cases.
- **Live app in Arabic and English:** 108 checks pass and none fail.
  - Closing without G6 is refused with 422 and nothing is written.
  - Access stays scoped: a user gets 404 outside their scope and holds no gate permission.
  - The `#0078FF` colour is marked provisional.
  - The edit form never offers "closed", and its hint names G6 in both languages.
  - Cursor tampering is refused with 400, and the identity routes behave correctly.

  I looked at the screenshots myself. The Arabic edit screen is right-to-left with the "مؤقت" (provisional) badge. The English detail screen is left-to-right and shows Unknown, never zero, for missing data. The playbook (`playbook.md:104`) defines G6 as Sustain, so tying closure to G6 is faithful to the source.
- **Fixed rules still hold:**
  - all 34 colour tokens are provisional;
  - no translation claims official PMI or Mobily status, or certification;
  - no external CDN;
  - the API spec lint and both type checks pass;
  - engineering gates DG0–DG7 never appear in the interface text.
- **Register:** all 8 assigned requirement rows are implemented with every evidence file present. The 29 other P1 rows due at later gates are marked specified only, so none is claimed as delivered.
- **Round-6 closures:** all 12 named findings (F-DG1-001/002/003/004/005/006/105/007/008/207/009/210) are verified closed and still hold, each backed by one of the checks above.

**Findings:** none new.
- One wording note, not a finding: D-053 lists "the round-7 reviews + auditor" as evidence the decision expects. It reads as a plan, not a claim that they already exist.
- F-DG1-127 and F-DG1-212 belong to the code-security and QA reviewers. I only checked the over-reach and regression side of 127, and I didn't change either status.

Files are in `docs/delivery/reviews/DG1/round-7/`:
- domain-reviewer.json — passes the review schema, and every evidence path exists

Evidence is in `docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG1/domain/round-7/`. I didn't write a findings or verifications file, because I own neither open finding. I grant no business, Finance or IT approval, and product gate G6 doesn't imply DG7.
